title: Observer: notify every subscriber
summary: Subscribers hand the feed a callback and get back a function that unsubscribes them. publish() loops over a copy of the list, so a callback can unsubscribe mid-publish without skipping its neighbour.
code: # The feed calls every subscriber without knowing what they do; it loops over a copy.
triggers: one change must reach many dependents, and the source shouldn't know who they are
subscribe and unsubscribe, listeners, event handlers: 'notify everyone when X changes'
prompts: When a flight's gate changes, the departure board, the mobile app and the crew pager all need the new gate. Next quarter a chat bot will want it too, and the gate system must not change.
A spreadsheet cell feeds several charts. Whenever the value changes every chart showing it redraws, and closing a chart stops its updates.
invariant: publish calls each callback that was subscribed when it started, exactly once, and the feed never depends on what a callback does.
mantra: Keep a list; notify a copy.
pitfalls: Loop over a copy: a callback that unsubscribes during publish would make the live loop skip its neighbour.
Unsubscribe removes this callback; forgotten subscriptions keep their objects alive.
A slow or failing callback holds up the rest; real systems queue or isolate them.
